title: kac type schema
description: The shape of a type file in `.schema/`. One file declares one record type: what it is called, where its records live, what their frontmatter carries, and what CI holds them to. The files beginning with an underscore are other shapes and this does not describe them.

type.description: The singular name of the type, as a record's frontmatter carries it.

label.description: How one record is named in generated prose: "Policy", "ADR", "NFR".

label-plural.description: How the collection is named: "Policies", "ADRs", "NFRs". Required where `label` is not, because nothing turns `nfr` into "NFRs".

folder.description: The folder holding this type's records, which is also what this file is named for: a document's type is inferred from its folder, so folder to schema is an identity lookup.

page.description: The type's own page, at the repository root. It carries the generated Metadata and What CI checks blocks.

tier.description: How a document of this type behaves. The vocabulary belongs to the `tier` field in `_universal.yaml`, and `_tiers.yaml` says what each value means.

lifecycle.description: Whether a record is superseded rather than rewritten, kept current, or left to go stale until something promotes it.

summary.description: What the type is, in one line, and it heads the type's row in the repository's own index. Rendered as a table cell, so `kac` holds it to a length, counted with whitespace folded.

goes-here.description: What a contributor has in hand when this type is the answer: "a rule people must follow when building". Rendered as a table cell, in the taxonomy's decision table.

detail.description: What the type carries beyond its first sentence, and the edge a reader is most likely to walk over. Rendered as prose rather than into a table, so no cell bound reaches it. It is the framework's account of the type: anything local, and any example from the estate, belongs on the type's own page.

collision.description: Where this type's name already means something else to a reader arriving from another framework. Say what the word means elsewhere and what the reader will get wrong. Paragraphs separated by a blank line, and links written inline rather than as reference labels. Most types collide with nothing and leave this out: inventing one spends a warning a reader would otherwise trust.

versus.description: The calls that are genuinely close, keyed by the other type. A pair is declared once, by the type its heading is titled from, and it renders as the taxonomy's disambiguation list. Which side declares it is a judgement, so a pair both sides declare fails, as does one against the declaring type itself. A pair renders only where the corpus adopted both types.

lineage.description: Where the type's name came from, and where it parts company with whatever lent it. This is the framework's own intellectual debt, identical wherever the schema is taken. What a corpus stands at against an external framework is the other thing entirely, and `frameworks.md` records it alone.

prior-art.description: What the type is nearest to, or that nothing established fits. Links are written inline, not as reference labels, because the block this renders into cannot see the definitions at the foot of the page it lands on. The only required part of the block, and "none" is one of its answers: claiming an ancestor a type has not got is worse than admitting none.

alignment.description: What the framework took from it. Leaving this and `divergence:` empty is a settled state for a type with no ancestor, and renders as an em dash.

divergence.description: Where the framework deliberately parts company.

id.description: How a record of this type is identified.

prefix.description: The prefix every id of this type carries, before the hyphen.

style.description: The shape of the id after the prefix: `numbered` is `width` digits, `mnemonic` is `width` upper-case alphanumerics opening with a letter, `slug` is lower-case words. Each is checked for its shape and then for agreement with the same discriminator in the filename.

width.description: How many characters a `numbered` or `mnemonic` discriminator carries, as an exact count or a `min`/`max` span. Defaults to 4. A `slug` has no fixed width and does not read it. A span is for `mnemonic` alone, whose length follows the concept it names, and it needs `filename.carries-id: false`, because several lengths cannot be read out of one filename. A `numbered` id is padded to one width so that ids sort.

min.description: The shortest discriminator this type admits.

max.description: The longest discriminator this type admits.

filename.description: What a record of this type may be called on disk.

pattern.description: What a record's filename must match, `.md` included.

carries-id.description: Whether the filename opens with the id's discriminator, as `0007-decide-x.md` and `vurm-remediation.md` do. Defaults to true. Set false where records are filed by topic alone, and then nothing reads the head of a filename as an id: not the agreement between the two, not the slug `slug-max` measures, and not the citation a link to the file would otherwise carry.

slug-max.description: The longest slug a filename may carry: the slug the author chose, so the extension is dropped and so is the discriminator where the name carries one ahead of it. Defaults to 30.

fields.description: The frontmatter this type adds to the universal fields, in the order a record writes them. A name declared in `_universal.yaml` too is a refinement of it.

sections.description: The H2 headings a record of this type carries.

required.description: Headings every record must carry, each holding something. A heading left bare fails as surely as one that is absent.

optional.description: Headings a record may carry. Held to holding something where it does.

index.description: The generated table on the type's page.

columns.description: The columns to render, in order. Each names a field the type declares or inherits.

sort.description: The columns to sort on, in order of precedence. The first breaks ties with the next. A scalar is the one-column case. Defaults to `id`, the one column every document carries.

order.description: Applied to the sort as a whole. Defaults to ascending.

parts.description: Where a record of this type keeps the parts something else may cite: the children a `pol-VURM.TIMEBOX` or `gls-knowledge-as-code.corpus` citation addresses. A type declaring no block offers no parts, and a citation into one of its records is reported as reaching nothing.

source.description: Where the parts are written. `table` reads the rows of the first table under the named section, each carrying its own id. `headings` reads the headings at `level` under it, each addressed by the anchor its heading slugs to.

section.description: The heading the parts sit under. Must be a section the type declares.

noun.description: What one part is called, used in the messages a citation failure reports: "clause", "term". Defaults to "part".

aside.description: The label a part's optional second block opens with, written bold: "Not" on a glossary term. An export carries the lead and the aside as two pieces. Omit where a type's parts carry no such block.

level.description: The heading level a part is written at, for `source: headings`. Defaults to 3.

columns.description: The table's headers, in order, for `source: table`. The first two are read positionally as the id and the part. Any further column is the type's own. Defaults to [Id, Clause].

id-pattern.description: What an authored part id must match, the half after the dot as `pol-VURM.TIMEBOX` carries it. Read for `source: table` only: a heading's id is derived from the heading rather than written.

binding.description: The modals written bold, which oblige. Ordered: rows appear in the order declared. `source: table` only.

advisory.description: The modals written plain, which recommend. They follow the binding ones. `source: table` only.

export.description: What a record of this type contributes to a published export, and how much of each piece travels. Its shape is a contract once a consumer corpus reads it. A type declaring no block contributes nothing.

version.description: The shape a consumer holds this type's exported files to. Moved by hand when a reader written against the shape before it would now be wrong: a key renamed or dropped, a value whose type changed, a key that means something new. Adding a key moves nothing. Each type carries its own, so a change to one type's shape cannot refuse a consumer reading another.

fields.description: The frontmatter a record contributes, in the order an export writes it. Each names a field the type declares or inherits, or `title`, which is the record's heading rather than a field. A field travels in the shape its declaration gives it: a list as a JSON array, anything else as a string.

sections.description: The sections that travel, keyed by the heading the type declares and each carrying the fidelity it travels at. A heading the `sections:` block does not declare fails: two structural declarations free to disagree are what selecting by key exists to prevent.

parts.description: What a record's parts contribute, and the shape of the line each one is written as. They are read from the type's `parts:` block, so a type exporting parts declares one.

fidelity.description: How much of each part travels. A line is already a reduction: `line:` below says key by key what of a part reaches a consumer.

line.description: The keys one part writes, in the order the line writes them, each naming the source that fills it. The key is the type's own word and reaches a consumer as written, so a glossary's `definition` and a policy's `level` never meet in one shape.

rules.description: What CI holds a record of this type to, beyond its fields and sections. Reciprocity, section mirroring and conditional requirement are declared on the field instead, and an entry restating one of those has no effect.

notes.description: Commentary: what these files should say and the tool has no use for. Admitted at every level and required at none. Where a field carries both, `description:` is what a reader of the type page needs at a glance and `notes:` is the reasoning there is no room for there. A field declaring only notes still renders them.

regex.description: A .NET regular expression, anchored, and quoted in YAML so the backslashes survive.

fidelity.description: How much of one piece travels into an export. `full` carries it whole, `summary` cuts it to its opening block, and `reference` carries the key and none of its words. Written against every entry and defaulted nowhere: which of the three a consumer gets is the whole of what an export declares.

lineSource.description: Where one key of a part line takes its value from. `part.lead` and `part.aside` read a part's body, which only a heading-sourced type gives a part: a table row is its own body, and a table-sourced type carries the row through `part.text` and its columns. `front.<field>` names a field the type declares or inherits. `column.<Header>` names a header the type's `parts.columns:` declares.

field.description: One frontmatter key, and everything asked of its value.

description.description: What a reader needs at a glance, in one line. Rendered into the generated Metadata table, which pads every column to its widest cell. Keep it under about 100 characters and leave the reasoning to `notes:`. An enum's `values:` are outside that budget, because they render in a small table of their own beneath it.

required.description: Whether every record must carry the key.

required-when.description: The condition under which an otherwise optional field must be filled in, as one test against one other field of the same document. Three forms and no others: `other == value`, `other != value`, `other in [a, b]`. Where the field it names is absent the condition does not hold, `!=` included.

type.description: What the value is. Defaults to `string`.

of.description: What each entry of a list is. `object` makes them mappings, and `entry:` then declares the keys one holds.

entry.description: The keys one entry of the list holds, where `of: object` makes its entries mappings. Declared with the vocabulary a field is declared with, so a key is held to its own `type:`, `pattern:` and `required:`. Order is load-bearing: the first key declared is the one naming the entry, which is what the entries are sorted on and what an index column renders.

values.description: An enum's range: written inline, or drawn from `_enums.yaml` as `$enums.<name>`.

ref.description: The folders an id in this field may belong to. A scalar is the one-folder case. Both halves are asked of every id: that it names a record, and that the record is of a type named here. An id of the wrong type lands on a real page and reads as deliberate, and this line is the only place the type it should have named is written down. A folder this corpus declined is left unenforced, and adopting the type starts the reference with no edit here.

part-required.description: Whether an id in this field must reach a part of the record rather than the record whole. A standard's `implements:` declares it, so it names the clauses it puts into practice one by one. The record named whole reads to anything walking the edge as every part covered. Needs a `ref:` to resolve the part against, and every type it names has to keep parts.

reciprocal.description: The field on the target that must point back. Every id is resolved against the corpus whether or not the edge is reciprocal, so this declares the return leg and nothing else.

pattern.description: A further constraint on the value, applied to each entry where the field is a list.

from.description: Where the field's value comes from, for a field the record never writes. `sub-path` is the folders between the type's own folder and the file, so `standards/platform/node/testing.md` carries `platform/node`. A record saved straight into its type folder gets an empty value. A derived field may not also be `required:`, and `derived-key` reports one written into frontmatter.

mirrors-section.description: The section whose ids this field must mirror. It must be one the type's `sections:` block declares. The ids are held in both directions and case-insensitively, in a bullet or in prose alike. Both directions is the part to weigh: the field has to be the whole truth about what the section names, so a prose aside about something deliberately absent from the field will fail.

mirrors-citations.description: The label on the footnote lines whose citations this field must mirror. Each line is written in italic with the label bold, and closes the section whose citations it gathers: `_**Covers:** [pol-SCRT].EMBED_`. A section covering nothing carries no line. The union of the lines is held equal to the field, in both directions and case-insensitively, so the field stays the whole truth about what the document answers. The field must declare a `ref:`, since the lines gather citations of another record.

allow-literal.description: Words admitted beside the field's declared type: `last-rehearsed: never`, `applies-to: [all]`. A value listed here is taken as written and nothing further is asked of it. On a list it exempts the entry rather than the field, so the ids beside it are still ids.

min-items.description: The floor on a list's length, for the field whose value is its breadth. A field the schema tells authors to over-fill is otherwise held to a single entry.

min-records.description: The floor on how many records carry a given value, for a field whose values group documents rather than describe one. Counted per type, case-insensitively, and once per record however often one repeats a value. Reports a warning against each record carrying the short value. The membership of the vocabulary is never declared here.

rule.description: One entry of a type's `rules:` block. A rule states an intention from the moment it is written, and it gains a `severity:` when something can act on it.

id.description: What dispatches the rule: an expression compiled here, or a rule class registered under the same name.

description.description: What is checked, in the schema's own words. Rendered into the type page's checks table. The reasoning belongs in `message:`.

severity.description: Whether tripping the rule fails a build or advises an author. Absent means declared and not enforced, which is the only state a rule nothing dispatches may hold.

expr.description: The condition a document must satisfy. A rule carrying one needs no C#. Absent on the rules that need a real algorithm, and on the rules nothing answers to yet.

message.description: What the author is told when the expression fails, a diagnosis where `description:` is a definition.

postures.description: The framework standings a roll-up rule holds a policy's `aligns-with` to, written as the corpus's own framework register heads them. A framework filed under any other standing may be cited by a clause and stays out of the roll-up.

max-words.description: The ceiling a Y-statement is held to.
